items.name: Gagosian
items.note: Blue-chip postwar and contemporary programme; 555 West 24th Street is the main Chelsea space in a global network of around twenty galleries.

items.name: White Cube Bermondsey
items.note: Opened 2011 at 144-152 Bermondsey Street and billed as Europe's largest commercial gallery space; contemporary programme rooted in the YBA generation plus international mid-career artists.

items.name: Hauser & Wirth Zurich
items.note: Founded in Zurich in 1992 and based in the Löwenbräukunst complex at Limmatstrasse 270; contemporary art plus major 20th-century estates, with a strong record on rediscovered women artists.

items.name: Perrotin Paris
items.note: Founded 1990 by Emmanuel Perrotin, in an 18th-century Marais townhouse at 76 rue de Turenne; contemporary programme with a notable East Asian roster and roughly ten international spaces.

items.name: Galleria Continua
items.note: Founded 1990 in a Tuscan hill town rather than a capital; deliberately internationalist programme that has since opened spaces in Beijing, Havana, Paris, São Paulo and Dubai.

items.name: Goodman Gallery
items.note: Founded 1966 with a significant anti-apartheid exhibition history; a leading platform for African and diaspora artists, now also in Cape Town, London and New York.

items.name: Gallery 1957
items.note: Opened on Ghana's independence day in 2016 inside the Kempinski Gold Coast City; focused on West African contemporary artists, with a second space in London.

items.name: kurimanzutto
items.note: Started in 1999 as a nomadic project and now housed in an Alberto Kalach-converted former lumberyard; central to Mexico City's contemporary scene with a broad Latin American roster.

items.name: Galeria Nara Roesler
items.note: Founded 1989; Brazilian modern and contemporary art including Geometric Abstraction and Neo-Concrete estates, with further spaces in Rio de Janeiro and New York.

items.name: ShanghART Gallery (West Bund)
items.note: Founded 1996 and among the earliest galleries for Chinese contemporary art; its West Bund space sits in Shanghai's riverside museum district.

items.name: Kukje Gallery
items.note: Founded 1982 in Samcheong-dong; brought major international artists to Korea and represents Dansaekhwa painters alongside contemporary Korean practices, across three buildings.

items.name: Chemould Prescott Road
items.note: Descended from Gallery Chemould, founded 1963 and among India's oldest commercial galleries; contemporary Indian and South Asian art from a heritage building in Fort.

items.name: Roslyn Oxley9 Gallery
items.note: Founded 1982 in Paddington; a leading Australian contemporary gallery that has built the international careers of artists including Tracey Moffatt, Fiona Hall and Patricia Piccinini.

items.name: Venice Biennale (Biennale Arte)
items.note: Biennial, even years; the art edition runs roughly mid-May to late November across the Giardini, the Arsenale and city-wide national pavilions. The 61st edition is 9 May-22 November 2026.

items.name: documenta
items.note: Quinquennial (every five years), running 100 days over the summer and centred on the Fridericianum. documenta 16 is 12 June-19 September 2027.

items.name: Sharjah Biennial
items.note: Biennial, odd years, run by Sharjah Art Foundation across multiple sites in the emirate; typically opens in late January or February and closes in June. SB17 is 21 January-13 June 2027.

items.name: Gwangju Biennale
items.note: Biennial, even years; Asia's oldest contemporary art biennial, usually running early September to mid-November from the Gwangju Biennale Exhibition Hall. The 16th edition is 5 September-15 November 2026.

items.name: Bienal de São Paulo
items.note: Biennial, odd years, in Niemeyer's Ciccillo Matarazzo Pavilion in Ibirapuera Park; opens in September and now runs into January. The 36th edition ran 6 September 2025-11 January 2026.

items.name: Dak'Art (Biennale of Contemporary African Art)
items.note: Biennial, even years, centred on the derelict Ancien Palais de Justice; recent editions have run in the November-December window. There is an artist open call each cycle, with applications usually opening in the spring before the edition.

items.name: Kochi-Muziris Biennale
items.note: Biennial, opening in December and running to late March or April across Fort Kochi, Mattancherry and Ernakulam, with Aspinwall House as the main hub. The sixth edition ran 12 December 2025-31 March 2026.

items.name: Biennale of Sydney
items.note: Biennial, even years, free to the public and typically running mid-March to mid-June. The 25th edition (14 March-14 June 2026) is anchored at White Bay Power Station with the Art Gallery of NSW and Western Sydney venues.

items.name: Istanbul Biennial
items.note: Biennial organised by İKSV, normally running in the autumn (roughly September to November) in repurposed buildings along the Beyoğlu-Karaköy axis. The 18th edition is exceptionally staged in three legs between 2025 and 2027.

items.name: Whitney Biennial
items.note: Biennial, even years; the longest-running survey of contemporary art in the United States, typically opening in March and closing in late summer. The 2026 edition runs 8 March-23 August.

items.name: Art Basel
items.note: Annual fair, held in June at Messe Basel with invited-collector preview days immediately beforehand; the benchmark event of the international art market, with around 290 galleries in 2026.

items.name: Frieze London
items.note: Annual fair, held each October in a temporary pavilion in The Regent's Park alongside Frieze Masters, with a free outdoor Frieze Sculpture display running for several weeks around it.

items.name: Zona Maco
items.note: Annual fair, held in early February at Centro Citibanamex and the anchor of Mexico City Art Week; around 200 galleries, weighted towards Mexico and Latin America.
